audit.why: 42.14% over 2105 games per packet — a genuinely hard matchup, matching diff HARD 8/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers held opposite blanket charts: full gave Fizz all 7 stages, content gave Mel all 7 (which the packet flags against the 42.14% WR). Both are wrong as blankets.
audit.why: Pre-6, melee Fizz must walk into Mel's 950-range poke to farm and has no kill threat (content whys 0-3 are grounded). From 6, Chum the Waters guarantees his combo and with ignite kills outright (content's own spikes[1]); first item and late, one landed R still deletes Mel — consistent with the 42% WR.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Mel levels 1-5 (rows 0-3), Fizz from Level 6 (rows 4-6), edited on BOTH layers as one atomic group with matching whys.

audit.why: Spikes are right: Mel's poke window 3-5, Fizz's decisive 6 (R 120s), first-item roam snowball, late one-combo threat. All 4 entries present.

audit.corrected: See edits: numbers in cooldowns, tell in tradeBad, projectile truth in dontsFull[2].d.

notes: The packet defect (all-Mel chart vs 42.14% WR) came from the content layer's blanket; the full layer's all-Fizz blanket was equally wrong. The claim that Rebuttal can return the Chum the Waters fish rests on the R's projectile derived-flag plus Mel's W text; whether a reflected fish re-attaches is not in Riot's text — unverified beyond 'blockable'.
